newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Ex Colombian army official linked to massacre.
newsitem.headline: Ex Colombian army official linked to massacre.

text.p: Authorities ordered the arrest Wednesday of a former Colombian army major linked to the murder of nine judicial officials killed while investigating a massacre more than eight years ago.
A spokesman for the prosecutor-general's office said a warrant for the arrest of Oscar de Jesus Echandia had been issued on grounds of his suspected involvement in "homicide for terrorist ends."

Echandia, who was recently deported from the United States at the request of Colombian authorities, was in active military service when the nine judicial officials were shot and killed by unidentified gunmen in northern Santander province in January 1989.
They had been probing the gangland-style murders of 19 merchants in the Magdalena Medio region of Santander at the time they were killed.

A retired army general, Farouk Yanine Diaz, was arrested last October on charges that he gave a right-wing death squad the go ahead to kill the merchants because they were suspected lefist rebel sympathisers.
Human rights groups say death squads, working with the tacit support of Colombia's military, have killed with impunity for decades.
No ruling has been handed down in the case of Yanine, who is being investigated by a military tribunal.
